[NDBG.1.2] **Several reads are only meaningful while the engine is paused** —
that is, between pumps, when the integrator's driver has stopped advancing the
engine and working memory is quiescent. Specifically: live occupancy in
`ds_engine_rete_network` ([NDBG.4.1]) and `ds_engine_get_justifiers`
([NDBG.5.2]). Reading them mid-pump yields a torn snapshot. A debugger tracks its
own paused state and gates these reads on it (the DAP bridge does exactly this).

The engine gates it too, and more broadly: the only way to be on the pump's
stack is from inside a callback, and **every** `ds_engine_*` call from there
returns `DS_ERR_STATE` ([RARC.13.16]) — reads included. So a mid-pump read is
refused rather than torn. A debugger's own paused-state tracking stays worth
having, because it keeps the debugger from asking a question it will be told to
stop asking.
